message:
36M. I got into poison ivy while clearing brush on Saturday. Itchy blistery rash on both forearms, spreading a bit within that area. No fever, no trouble breathing.

Additional patient information: The rash is still only on my forearms. The itch is mild and does not affect sleep. No face, eye or genital involvement, no increasing pain or pus.

output.reason: Localized, mildly itchy vesicular rash confined to both forearms after known poison ivy exposure, with no fever, no breathing trouble, no face/eye/genital involvement and no increasing pain or pus reported; no decision-critical clinician task is established, so guidance plus an action-based safety net is sufficient.
output.patientMessage: I recommend self-care at home with over-the-counter measures from your pharmacist for this poison ivy rash. It is limited to your forearms, the itch is mild, and you report no fever or breathing trouble, so no clinician assessment is needed right now. Message Counsel if the rash spreads well beyond your forearms, reaches your face, eyes or genitals, becomes painful or starts draining pus, or if fever develops. Seek emergency care for any trouble breathing or facial/throat swelling.
differential: Allergic contact dermatitis from urushiol (poison ivy), consistent with reported exposure and vesicular forearm rash
Secondary bacterial skin infection — no increasing pain or pus reported, remains possible later
Apparent spread from delayed sensitization rather than new exposure
